title: Chicken Parmesan a la Foyot
description:
This recipe is adapted from “60-Minute Gourmet” and is an example of how “great French cooking need not
take hours and days of preparation to be brought to simple perfection.” In French, it was called Cotês de Veau
Foyot, named after the greatest restaurant in Paris in the middle of the 19th century. Here, we’re substituting
Veau (veal) with boneless, skinless chicken thighs, maybe calling it Cuisses de Poulet Foyot.
This dish is still suitable for your most discriminating friends – or family! – maybe with some noodles and a fresh
tomato sauce. It’s also reminiscent of Chicken Parmesan, but easier, especially for a bigger group.
ingredients: One regular chicken thigh will yield about 3 ounces of meat (without skin or bone), so for big meat eaters, count
8 to 12+ boneless skinless chicken thighs (see above)
1 cup grated Parmesan (maybe with Locatelli Romano)
1 cup dry white wine, or vermouth, or chicken broth, or water
directions: on two thighs per person. For kids and lighter eaters, one chicken thigh per person should be enough.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees.
Sprinkle the thighs on both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat 2-4 tablespoons olive oil in a heavy skillet, then add the garlic cloves and
thighs.
Cook over medium high heat until golden brown on one side, about 1-3 minutes,
depending on the thigh sizes (little organic ones – just barely 2 minutes; regular
grocery store ones – about 3 minutes).
Turn the chicken and cook similarly until golden brown on the other side.
Transfer the thighs to a sheet pan, smooth side down, and keep warm.
Pour off most of the rendered fact from the pan and deglaze it with the wine,
scrapping up all the tasty little bits. Pour this little sauce into the sheet pan,
around and over the thighs.
Meanwhile, blend the breadcrumbs, cheese, and butter with your hands or a fork,
until thoroughly mixed together and blended.
Work the mixture into sheets of topping on each thigh. (If you have extra, just eat
a few “pinches of heaven” or add it to the tomato sauce before serving.)
Place sheet pan with dressed chicken thighs, uncovered, in the oven and bake about 10 minutes until the
tops are appetizingly brown and cooked thoroughly (165 degrees if you want to check).
You can serve the chicken with a little of the sauce or add the liquid to the pasta and tomato sauce.
